summary:
We developed LUNARIS as an interactive web application that helps users explore and compare potential regions around the Moon's south pole for future lunar missions. It integrates NASA-derived scientific datasets, including historical sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and lunar terrain information. The application features an interactive lunar map, 3D Moon visualization, site comparison, illustrative simulations, and downloadable PDF reports.

LUNARIS addresses the challenge of making complex lunar exploration data accessible, understandable, and easier to compare. By combining different scientific datasets into one platform, users can examine environmental conditions while understanding the sources, coverage, and limitations of the information.

This project is important because future lunar exploration involves challenges such as limited sunlight, communication visibility, and difficult terrain. LUNARIS supports scientific education and informed exploration by transforming complex data into interactive visual information. Ultimately, it aims to help students, educators, and researchers better understand the lunar environment and the considerations involved in future Moon missions.
details:
Our project, LUNARIS, is an educational lunar south-pole planning explorer designed to make scientific information about the Moon more accessible and understandable.

It integrates NASA-derived datasets, including historical sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and lunar terrain information, into an interactive web application. Users can explore nine Artemis III candidate regions, examine terrain through 3D visualization, compare different locations and date intervals, and generate PDF reports.

The main benefit of our project is that it brings different types of scientific information together in one platform, helping students, educators, and researchers better understand the environmental conditions of the lunar south pole.

What makes our project creative is the combination of scientific data processing, interactive mapping, 3D visualization, and simulation features.

During development, we considered scientific transparency, data availability, terrain conditions, sunlight, Earth visibility, accessibility, and user experience.

Ultimately, our goal is to support education and research by making lunar exploration data easier to understand, explore, and communicate.

NASA PGDA Product 69 — long-term lunar illumination and Earth-visibility data
